Therefore, results will be described in general terms across the four metrics for flexibility potential. The Full tariff (first panel) offers the most potential followed by Medium and Mild. Larger end use resources such as residential space cooling, and Level 1 and Level 2 EV charging do not exhibit significant changes between the three levels of potential (technical, cost effective, and short payback). This is because the cost to enable load response within these end uses is relatively low, with essentially all customers meeting the short payback threshold. Thus, the differences between the levels of potential are observed within the smaller end use resources such as commercial space heating and cooling, residential space heating, and spa pumps. These differences are much less apparent in the Full tariff scenario, which is effective in realizing almost all of the technical potential within a short payback period. 44 Figure 29. Technical, cost effective, and short payback potential across end uses and price designs, quantified by four metrics: bill savings (top row), grid avoided costs (second row), shed potential (third row), and avoided emissions (bottom row) 45 One resource where cost effectiveness and short paybacks are not always met is commercial space cooling in the Medium- and Mild-Low tariff scenarios. This end use offers a bill savings technical potential of about 390 million USD (2024$), most of which is cost effective. However, requiring a short payback period of 3 years or less, causes a reduction of about 40% (Medium tariff scenario), with total bill savings of only 246 million USD. The remaining cost effective potential (~144 million USD) is available over a longer payback period. We find that this reduction is primarily in medium and large commercial customers in hot-dry climate zones and is due to higher technology costs that are assumed to scale with the peak demand of the end use. Large commercial customers in marine climate zone also have a hard time meeting short payback requirements, as their cooling loads are quite low and therefore the bill savings are about half as much as their counterparts with a short payback period. Finally, in the mild tariff scenario, the cost effective potential is half of the technical potential, and the short payback potential is about a quarter of technical potential. Table 5.
